about.title: Palm Desert Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Palm Desert residents rely on a mix of local clinics, urgent care centers, and larger Coachella Valley hospitals for treatment, and most of the time care goes as expected. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is administered incorrectly, the effects can be serious and lasting. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there are shorter notice windows, a requirement for expert medical review, and specific rules about what damages can be recovered. LawProactive doesn't practice law or evaluate your medical records ourselves; instead, we connect you at no cost with an independent attorney in our network who handles these claims and can tell you honestly whether what happened to you may qualify as malpractice. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Deadlines Are Short
items.desc: California generally requires malpractice claims within one year of discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider — missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to confirm that a provider's care fell below the accepted standard; an independent attorney can help arrange this kind of review.

items.title: Damages Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California caps non-economic damages in malpractice cases, though the cap rises each year, and understanding how it applies takes someone familiar with current MICRA figures.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result alone isn't proof of malpractice; the question is whether the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard. An attorney working with a medical expert can help sort out whether that standard was met.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim if something went wrong at a Palm Desert medical facility?
items.answer: Generally you have one year from when you discover the harm, capped at three years from the date of the injury, and a 90-day notice must go to the provider before filing suit. These deadlines are strict, so it helps to talk to someone promptly rather than wait.

items.question: What does it cost to find out if I have a case?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your claim results in a recovery.
